Cancer-Gene Carrier Penetrance & Variant-Classification Concordance

All of Us (AoU) Researcher Workbench · crude, cross-sectional, single-cohort estimates

This analysis asks two questions of the same AoU carrier cohort: (1) among people carrying a likely-pathogenic variant in a cancer-predisposition gene, what fraction actually develop the matched cancer, and at what age (penetrance); and (2) does the standard practice of relying on ClinVar to confirm pathogenicity work equally well across ancestries (ACMG vs ClinVar concordance). The headline finding is an equity gap, not a biology finding: automated ACMG classification flags many more likely-pathogenic variants than ClinVar has independently confirmed, and this gap is far larger for non-European ancestries — meaning ClinVar-only pipelines under-ascertain risk carriers outside European-ancestry populations. Separately, penetrance for well-established gene–cancer pairs (BRCA1/BRCA2 → breast & ovarian cancer) behaves as expected: carrier rates are far above population background and rise with age.

Background — definitions

Penetrance (as used here)
Of the people carrying a likely-pathogenic variant in a gene, the fraction who have the matched cancer type recorded in this cohort, by age band. This is a crude, cross-sectional proportion — not a survival/cumulative-incidence estimate, and not adjusted for follow-up time or competing risks.
ACMG/AMP P/LP
"Pathogenic / Likely Pathogenic" classification assigned automatically from the variant's own features (rule-based criteria), independent of any external database.
ClinVar P/LP
A public database of manually-submitted, lab-reviewed variant classifications. Submissions are historically concentrated on variants seen in European-ancestry sequencing efforts, so absence from ClinVar more often reflects under-study than true benignity.

Carrier definition used throughout this report: every penetrance number below counts a "carrier" as someone with an ACMG-PLP variant in that gene — not ClinVar-PLP, and not "any variant in the gene" (that broader set includes benign/VUS calls and would understate penetrance). We use ACMG rather than ClinVar specifically because Finding 1 shows ClinVar confirmation is far less complete for non-European carriers of the same real variants; restricting to ClinVar-PLP would reproduce that same ancestry bias inside the penetrance numbers.

How the numbers are calculated

Canonical carriers
The one agreed-upon carrier list per gene that every table and figure in this report is built from — instead of each analysis deriving its own, slightly different count. Built by a fixed chain, applied identically every time: (1) start from every variant row for the gene; (2) collapse to one entry per person per gene; (3) restrict to carriers of an ACMG-PLP variant; (4) join to the cohort table to get age/sex/phenotype — carriers with no matching cohort record are dropped here, and that drop is counted and reported, never silent; (5) restrict to the correct sex if the gene's cancer type(s) are sex-specific. Whatever count survives step 5 is used, unchanged, as the denominator for every downstream number for that gene.
Penetrance calculation
A carrier is only counted as "affected" if their recorded disease Group matches the gene's own mapped cancer type(s) (e.g. BRCA1 → breast or ovarian) — a BRCA1 carrier with lung cancer is not counted as a BRCA1 penetrance event. People recorded only under "Family history" (no personal diagnosis) are explicitly excluded from the numerator by an assertion in the code.
p̂gene,cancer,age  =  N(canonical carriers with that matched cancer)N(all canonical carriers in that age band)
Background (population baseline) rate
Computed over the entire cohort, not just carriers of the gene in question, with the same sex restriction applied as the carrier side so the comparison is apples-to-apples:
r̂bg, disease, age  =  N(whole cohort with that exact disease)N(whole cohort in that age band)
A carrier rate is marked ★ significantly elevated only when:
CIlower(carrier rate)  >  CIupper(background rate)
— a conservative non-overlapping-interval test, not just "the bar is taller." Because this cohort is a case/control/family-history study design rather than a random population sample, this background reflects the cohort's own case-mix, not a true general-population incidence rate.
Confidence intervals
Every proportion above (penetrance, background rate, and the concordance/discordance rate in Finding 1) uses a 95% Wilson score interval, not the simpler normal approximation — several cells here have small N or proportions near 0/1, where the normal approximation undercoverages and can produce bounds outside [0,1]:
CI  =  p̂ + z2/2n  ±  z√(p̂(1−p̂)/n + z2/4n2) 1 + z2/n
z = 1.96 (95% level), n = the denominator count in the matching formula above. Computed via statsmodels.stats.proportion.proportion_confint(method="wilson").

Finding 1 — the equity finding

Relying on ClinVar alone to confirm pathogenicity misses a much larger share of real carriers in non-European ancestry groups: discordance (ACMG-PLP but not confirmed ClinVar-PLP) is 42.5% in EUR vs. up to 90.9% in EAS, with confidence intervals for every non-EUR group not overlapping EUR.

*Singleton fraction = share of discordant variant instances carried by only one person in this dataset (a proxy for allele-count-1 rarity). Low singleton fractions mean discordance is mostly driven by recurrent variants, not one-off rare calls — consistent with a real curation gap rather than noise. Exception: EAS discordance (90.9%) is dominated by a single recurrent MSH6 variant (83.5% of all EAS discordant instances) — this specific number should be read as "one variant's classification status," not broad-based under-curation across many EAS variants.

Finding 2 — penetrance behaves as expected

BRCA1 (n=320 canonical female carriers): breast and ovarian cancer rates rise with age and sit far above population background at every age band — consistent with known BRCA1 biology, and lower than clinic-ascertained penetrance estimates, as expected for an unselected population cohort.

BRCA2 (n=705 canonical female carriers): same pattern, at consistently lower absolute rates than BRCA1 — matching the known BRCA1 > BRCA2 ordering for breast/ovarian cancer risk.

BRCA1 and BRCA2 are shown as the headline pair because they have the largest canonical carrier counts (320 and 705 respectively) and therefore the tightest confidence intervals — not because other genes were excluded. The same chart for every other interpretable gene is below.

Limitations

  • Crude, cross-sectional, not survival-adjusted. Penetrance here is a point-in-time proportion within an age band, not a cumulative-incidence or Kaplan–Meier estimate; it does not account for variable follow-up time.
  • All of Us is not population-representative. It is a healthcare-utilizing, opt-in volunteer cohort; cancer-predisposition gene carriers who never sought care, or who died before enrollment, are not captured, and case ascertainment overall is subject to selection bias.
  • Denominator reconciliation. 216 BRCA1 carriers (30.3%) had no matching cohort/phenotype record and were dropped before any penetrance calculation; see carrier_filter_log.tsv for the full per-gene breakdown.
  • Some genes excluded for pseudogene-mapping artifacts (notably PMS2) — see exclusion table above.
  • Small cells excluded. Gene x ancestry cells (canonical denominator): 162 Cells below min_carriers=3: 62 Evidence gap: 38.3% of gene x ancestry cells have fewer than 3 carriers.
  • These results are preliminary, single-cohort, and not validated against an independent dataset.

What this sets up

The concordance gap motivates ancestry-aware variant classification — ClinVar-only pipelines should not be trusted as a sole confirmation step outside European-ancestry populations, and ACMG-flagged variants lacking ClinVar support in non-EUR carriers are a natural re-curation priority list. The penetrance pipeline built here (canonical denominator, disease-matched numerator, population-background comparison) is the basis for the next step: variant-level, competing-risk-adjusted absolute risk estimation.
